fr.plain: Une fois fini, le travail est {}
poussé, mais pas mis en ligne

slots.when: The draft asks the agent to finish, wrap up or resume work in a project whose result reaches people only after a push, deploy, release or publish, and neither the draft nor the conversation says whether the agent may take that last step.
slots.settled: The draft or a Decisions line says to ship or to stop short ("build and deploy", "keep it local"); the user already granted shipping, or the conversation shows the agent merging or deploying; there is no outward step; or the user is answering the agent.
slots.why: A deploy puts unreviewed work in front of users at once, while stopping short leaves a finished fix unshipped and costs another round trip.
slots.source: MarginCue owner history, authoring half; Saltzer and Schroeder 1975, fail-safe defaults

slots.when: The draft has the agent write an email, message, reply, comment or post that the agent could send or publish itself through a connected account or tool, and the draft does not say whether the agent sends it or hands back a draft.
slots.settled: The draft says who sends ("draft only", "I'll send it", "post it"); the user is approving or editing a draft the agent already showed; a standing instruction covers sending; or the agent has no way to send.
slots.why: A sent message or public post cannot be recalled, while a draft that was meant to go out leaves people waiting for an answer.

slots.when: The draft asks for a message or question that could go privately to one person or publicly to a shared channel, forum, tracker or thread, who can read it matters (a personal request, a complaint, an unreleased detail), and the draft does not say which.
slots.settled: The draft names the channel or recipients, or says private or public; only one channel exists; the user is replying inside an existing thread; or the user has already chosen where to send it.
slots.why: A question posted where others can read it cannot be made private again and may expose a request meant for one person.

slots.when: The draft mentions material or records that live in the user's own external account (mailbox, messaging app, calendar, cloud drive, task manager) that the agent can reach through a browser or connector, without saying whether the agent may open, fetch from or change that account.
slots.settled: The draft grants or withholds access ("you may fetch it", "update my calendar", "don't touch my mail"); a standing instruction covers that account; the material is already in the workspace; or the request plainly requires reading there, such as summarising what changed.
slots.why: Acting in a personal account can expose or change private data, while holding back leaves the agent waiting for files it could have fetched.
slots.source: MarginCue owner history, authoring half; Saltzer and Schroeder 1975, least privilege

slots.when: The draft states a new rule or limit for recurring entries (calendar events, records, uploads, files, names) while entries made under the old practice already exist, and does not say whether those existing entries are changed or only new ones must follow it.
slots.settled: The draft says "from now on" or "fix the existing ones", or its wording covers what exists ("everywhere"); a Decisions line fixes it; no old entries exist; the rule constrains a deliverable still being made; or the user is answering the agent.
slots.why: Applying a rule to existing entries rewrites data people rely on, while applying it only forward leaves the exceptions the user may have meant to remove.

fr.expert: La portée du retour arrière est {}

en.plain: reverting and deleting what was created

fr.plain: tout défaire et supprimer les créations

slots.when: The draft asks to cancel, stop, undo or roll back ("undo all that", "cancel it") while the agent has both running work and lasting effects (edited files, created or shared resources, sent changes), and does not say which of these to reverse.
slots.settled: The draft names what to reverse or keep ("just stop the job", "revert the files too"); a Decisions line fixes it; only one thing could be undone; or the user is picking from the agent's own list of undo options.
slots.why: Reverting or deleting more than intended destroys hours of work and items others use, while only stopping may leave unwanted edits in place.

fr.plain: seulement ce qui ne sert plus

en.plain: only items made in this task

fr.plain: seulement ce que j'ai créé ici
fr.expert: les artefacts créés par la tâche

slots.when: The draft asks to delete, prune or clean up items named by a loose category (old, unused, temporary, duplicate, test) where some items sit on the boundary, such as ones still referenced, recently used or owned by others, and the line is not drawn.
slots.settled: The draft or a Decisions line gives an exact rule or list (paths, a name pattern, an age); the items sit in a scratch area the agent created; the removal is a text edit in a draft; or it is reversible, such as archiving.
slots.why: Deleting an item that is still referenced or belongs to someone else breaks it with no undo, while keeping too much leaves the clutter the user wanted gone.
slots.source: reasoned; the dry-run option that destructive command-line tools commonly offer

fr.plain: Les lancements coûteux en attente sont {}
fr.expert: Les tâches coûteuses en attente sont {}

slots.when: The draft resumes, continues or approves work while queued or planned runs would cost real money, quota or hours of exclusive machine time (paid compute, long benchmark jobs, bulk API calls), and it does not say whether those runs start now.
slots.settled: The draft names which runs to start or hold; the user already approved the launch; the draft meets the condition the agent set for launching, such as a resource now being free; the pending steps are cheap; or no costly run is in view.
slots.why: A launched run spends money, quota or machine hours that cannot be recovered, while holding it stalls work the user expected to find done.

en.plain: a small trial, then I ask

fr.plain: un petit essai, puis je demande

slots.when: The draft starts or extends open-ended work that pays per use beyond the normal session (cloud compute, pay-per-call APIs, purchased credits, a paid service), and sets no limit, so the agent must choose how much to spend before stopping.
slots.settled: The draft or a Decisions line sets a cap, a share of credits, a number of runs or a stopping rule; the user says there is no cap or wants credits used up before they expire; or the work is a single bounded call.
slots.why: An uncapped loop can burn a month of credits overnight, while a cap set too low stops the run before it shows anything.

fr.expert: Les décisions en cours de tâche sont {}

slots.when: The draft hands over an open-ended, multi-hour task with licence for large changes (big refactors, many experiments, heavy token use), and says nothing about whether the agent should stop for approval at major forks or decide alone and keep going.
slots.settled: The draft delegates ("carte blanche", "you decide", "don't ask") or asks for check-ins ("ask me before merging", named checkpoints); a standing instruction covers autonomy; or the task is a bounded change, a question or a suggestion.
slots.why: Stopping to ask can leave an unattended run idle for hours, while deciding alone can spend the whole budget on a direction the user would have vetoed.
slots.source: MarginCue owner history, authoring half; Parasuraman, Sheridan and Wickens 2000, levels of automation

en.plain: a new direction, ignoring old pages

fr.plain: une nouvelle direction, sans les anciennes

slots.when: The draft asks to redesign or substantially improve one part of a product, site or document while the rest shares the old look or approach, and does not say whether the other parts are a model to follow or also due for replacement.
slots.settled: The draft says to match the existing style, or names a reference to follow or to avoid; the rest of the product is an approved design system; or the change is a small fix inside a design the user accepts.
slots.why: Copying the look the user wants to replace makes the redesign inherit what they disliked, and the work is redone.

en.expert: the complete build in one pass

fr.expert: la version complète en une passe

slots.when: The draft asks for a new or wholly redone result whose look or creative direction is a matter of taste (a page, a redesign, a slide deck, a public piece) and takes hours to build, without saying whether to show a mockup or sample first.
slots.settled: The draft asks for a preview first or says to build it all directly; the user already approved a mockup or direction; the change adds to an approved design; or the result is functional and small enough to review whole.
slots.why: A full build in the wrong direction wastes hours of work and review, while a preview costs a short pause.

slots.when: The draft adds new content (a post, an article, a guide, release notes) to an existing site or document with a main page and room for separate sections, and does not say whether it goes into the existing page or a section of its own.
slots.settled: The draft names the location (a path, a section, "a new page for articles"); the site already has one obvious home for that kind of content; or the content replaces an existing item in place.
slots.why: Content put in the wrong place reshapes a public site in a way the user then has to undo, links included.

slots.when: The draft sets up a recurring search, watch, digest or alert from criteria the user gave, and real items will straddle them (a date window they partly overlap, a nearby region, an adjacent tier or category), without saying how to treat borderline items.
slots.settled: The draft or a Decisions line says to include or exclude near matches; the criteria are exact identifiers with no boundary; or the user is answering the agent's question about the criteria.
slots.why: A strict filter silently drops items the user would have wanted, while a loose one fills every digest with noise they stop reading.
